author: Staff Reporter
title: Coffeehouse Event Aims to Recruit Advocates for Foster Children in Milam County - NewsBreak
text:
By Staff Reporter ,
7 hours ago Community members interested in making a direct impact on the lives of children in foster care are invited to attend an informal meet-and-greet hosted by CASA of Milam County and the Milam Arts Society later this month.
The “CASA Café Meet & Greet” will take place Monday, Jan. 12, at 7 p.m. at Moon Brew Coffee Co. in Rockdale. The event is designed to introduce the public to the work of Court Appointed Special Advocates, known as CASA volunteers, who serve as independent voices for children navigating the foster care system.
Board members and current CASA advocates will be on hand to explain the role of a volunteer advocate, answer questions and share personal experiences from the field. Attendees can learn how CASA volunteers work with judges, caseworkers and families to help ensure children have safe, permanent homes.
Organizers say no prior legal or social work experience is required to become a CASA volunteer. Training is provided, and the primary qualification is a willingness to advocate for the best interests of a child.
The event is open to anyone curious about CASA’s mission, whether they are ready to begin the volunteer process or simply want more information. Coffee and conversation will provide a relaxed setting for learning about the program and its impact in Milam County.
CASA of Milam County serves children who have experienced abuse or neglect, helping guide them through court proceedings and life-changing decisions. Organizers say community involvement is critical to ensuring every child has a dedicated advocate.
Moon Brew Coffee Co. is located in Rockdale. Admission to the event is free.
